Hanna Domagala, Sr Project Manager, 879115 Ontario Inc
notes: Hanna Domagala, Sr Project Manager from 879115 Ontario Inc appeared virtually before the Committee to share concerns regarding the proposed closing of the Lancaster Street and Highway 85 ramp, noting that this will increase traffic on the Bridgeport ramps, which are already difficult to turn left/east from. H. Domagala urged Council to consider the necessity of this project and the impact it will have.

items.title: TSD-TRP-23-002, Lancaster Street and Highway 85 Ramp Closure Environmental Assessment Study – Recommendation
notes:
Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner Transportation Services, introduced the report, explaining that from a Ministry of Transportation (MTO) standpoint, the Lancaster ramps are not performing well, mostly due to collisions. M. Goetzke also noted that the ramps have relatively low usage compared to others, and that the closure of these ramps would provide an opportunity for a critical cycling connection to be implemented. M. Goetzke provided an overview of the public engagement that has taken place, including roughly 700 survey responses.

In response to the Committee, M. Goetzke noted that the risk of deferring this decision could potentially be missing the window of opportunity with MTO. The Committee expressed concerns with the lack of engagement with Kitchener City Councillors.

CAO-REC-23-001, Indigenous Space Needs Final Report (Staff Presentation)
notes:
Paula Whitlow, Director, Truth and Reconciliation provided a presentation on the report, which included an overview of the project goals and engagement process. P. Whitlow shared that common themes for space attributes included an accessible physical indoor space, cultural and sustaining opportunities on the natural land, and wrap-around services. P. Whitlow noted that staff are excited to continue to build momentum in the community and explore options for a way forward, working towards reconciliation and establishing authentic long term relationships.

A copy of the presentation is attached to the minutes. This report was received for information.

In response to the Committee, P. Whitlow shared that the needs are varied and that sharing a space with other groups is not off the table, although was not specifically mentioned during the engagement process. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, Kara McLean, Head, External Stakeholder Management, confirmed that the work was done on behalf of all area municipalities and that there was representation from all municipalities. K. McLean explained that the report looks at how as a community we can respond to the diverse needs, which includes looking to the private sector.

items.title: PDL-ECD-23-003, Charles Street Terminal Visioning Process, Community Consultation and Environmental Findings Update (Staff Presentation)
notes:
Matthew Chandy, Director Innovation and Economic Development and Sarah Millar, Manager, Land Portfolio provided a presentation on the Charles Street terminal visioning process, which included an overview of the history of the land, the technical and engagement work completed, and next steps for 2023. S. Millar noted that 2023 will include more stakeholder engagement, including the creation of five community connector roles. M. Chandy stated that this site is an opportunity to advance four shared community opportunities, which are, affordable housing, climate action, equity, diversity and inclusion, and a thriving economy. 

A copy of the presentation is attached to the minutes. This report was received for information. 

In response to the Committee, Rod Regier, Commissioner Planning, Development and Legislative Services confirmed that staff will come back to Council with a proposed strategy for facilitating the development of the site. R. Regier noted that Council would have the opportunity to sell the terminal outright with no conditions, if desired, but that Council does have the right to determine what the scope would be, in collaboration with the City of Kitchener. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, M. Chandy explained that specific outreach for different community groups is planned for 2023, including Indigenous groups, and that staff will reach out to City of Kitchener staff to determine how they can specifically target groups, such as condo boards.

items.title: PDL-CPL-23-003, Year-End 2022 Population and Household Estimates for Waterloo Region (Staff Presentation)
notes:
Danielle De Fields, Director, Community Planning provided a presentation, which provided an overview of how the Region will grow over the next 30 years, including a population forecast and housing mix. 

A copy of the presentation is attached to the minutes. This report was received for information.

M. Harris joined at 1:58 p.m.

In response to the Committee, R. Regier noted that the Bill 23 target of 7,000 new homes will be a challenge. R. Regier stated that the necessary land is available, but that the market may have a challenge in delivering those homes due to supply chain issues and labour shortage.

items.title: Verbal Update: ION LRT Winter Operations
notes:
M. Goetzke and Keolis staff provided a verbal update on the ION LRT winter operations, explaining that the Region owns the network and Keolis maintains and operates it.

Richard Dean from Keolis, noted that this particular winter has been very challenging for the team due to freezing rain and ice accumulation. R. Dean provided an overview of potential solutions, such as a scraping device, painting deicing fluid onto the wire, and shuttle buses, as well as their respective benefits and challenges. R. Dean stressed the importance of learning, and making adjustments and improvements as we learn and work on the process. 

This verbal update was received for information.

In response to the Committee, R. Dean noted that continuous service would help to keep ice off the line, however, maintenance needs must be factored in as well.

motions.item_title: PDL-LEG-23-012, Approval to Expropriate Lands (2nd Report) at 2322 Snyder’s Road East, in the Township of Wilmot
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the expropriation of lands for the purpose of significant soil management needs associated with long term landfill development and operation for the remaining life of the Waterloo landfill (Site) as detailed in report PDL-LEG-23-012 dated March 7, 2023, described as follows: Fee Simple Full Taking: Part Lot 1, Concession North of Snyder's Road, Wilmot, Part 5 on 58R-6613; subject to 1077502 and 399983, being all of PIN 22184 - 0195 (LT), in the Township of Wilmot ( 2322 Snyder’s Road (formerly known as 2320 Snyder’s Road East)); And that staff be instructed to register a Plan of Expropriation for the property within three months of the granting of the approval to expropriate the property, as required by the Expropriations Act; And that the registered owners be served with a Notice of Expropriation and a Notice of Possession for the property after the registration of the Plan of Expropriation and the Regional Solicitor is authorized to take any and all actions required to enforce such Notices including but not limited to any application pursuant to Section 40 of the Expropriations Act; And that the Regional Solicitor is authorized to enter into an agreement with the registered owners, or to make an application under Section 39 of the Expropriations Act, to adjust the date for possession specified in the Notice of Possession as may be required; And that if no agreement as to compensation is made with an owner, the statutory Offer of Compensation and payment be served upon the registered owners of the property in the amount of the market value of the interests in the land as estimated by the Region’s appraiser in accordance with the Expropriations Act ; And that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to execute any Indemnity agreement or other document related to payment of the statutory Offer of Compensation; And further that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof, upon the registration on title of the required documentation to complete the transaction or if determined by the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services that such lands, or any part or interest thereof, are not required for the subject Project as outlined in report PDL-LEG-23-012, dated March 7, 2023 .
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the expropriation of lands for the purpose of significant soil management needs associated with long term landfill development and operation for the remaining life of the Waterloo landfill (Site) as detailed in report PDL-LEG-23-012 dated March 7, 2023, described as follows:

Fee Simple Full Taking:

Part Lot 1, Concession North of Snyder's Road, Wilmot, Part 5 on 58R-6613; subject to 1077502 and 399983, being all of PIN 22184-0195 (LT), in the Township of Wilmot (2322 Snyder’s Road (formerly known as 2320 Snyder’s Road East));

And that staff be instructed to register a Plan of Expropriation for the property within three months of the granting of the approval to expropriate the property, as required by the Expropriations Act;

And that the registered owners be served with a Notice of Expropriation and a Notice of Possession for the property after the registration of the Plan of Expropriation and the Regional Solicitor is authorized to take any and all actions required to enforce such Notices including but not limited to any application pursuant to Section 40 of the Expropriations Act;

And that the Regional Solicitor is authorized to enter into an agreement with the registered owners, or to make an application under Section 39 of the Expropriations Act, to adjust the date for possession specified in the Notice of Possession as may be required;

And that if no agreement as to compensation is made with an owner, the statutory Offer of Compensation and payment be served upon the registered owners of the property in the amount of the market value of the interests in the land as estimated by the Region’s appraiser in accordance with the Expropriations Act;

And that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to execute any Indemnity agreement or other document related to payment of the statutory Offer of Compensation;

And further that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof, upon the registration on title of the required documentation to complete the transaction or if determined by the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services that such lands, or any part or interest thereof, are not required for the subject Project

as outlined in report  PDL-LEG-23-012, dated March 7, 2023.
